native_ownership.responsibility: Implement, debug, refactor, review, or test full-stack Blazor applications across Razor components, render modes, ASP.NET Core, persistence, JavaScript interop, and bUnit/Playwright coverage
excludes: Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by frontend-implement: Implement a frontend feature that does not involve Razor components or Blazor runtime behavior
Work whose primary requested outcome is owned by backend-refactor: Refactor existing backend code in .NET, ASP.NET Core, Node.js, Bun, NestJS, Elysia, TypeScript, or JavaScript applications

risk.rationale: The contract requires explicit repository and runtime safety evidence; mutation authority remains limited to the user's requested scope.

positive.prompt: Fix a Blazor page where UI hiding is the only authorization, prerender triggers a duplicate side effect, reconnect replays a command, and concurrent component work shares one DbContext. Respect the pinned .NET render-mode capabilities.

Add bUnit/integration/browser coverage for a Blazor component across prerender-to-interactive transition, circuit reconnect, server authorization, and JS interop disposal in the installed target framework.

negative.prompt: Implement a framework-neutral frontend page; the repository has no Razor components or Blazor hosting/runtime behavior.
Please produce this deliverable: Refactor existing backend code in .NET, ASP.NET Core, Node.js, Bun, NestJS, Elysia, TypeScript, or JavaScript applications. Verify the affected behavior.

scenarios.prompt: Fix a pinned-.NET Blazor page where UI hiding is the only authorization, prerender duplicates a side effect, circuit reconnect replays a command, and concurrent component tasks share one DbContext. Verify the actual render mode capability.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the answer within blazor-development's stated responsibility and does not recreate native Codex orchestration.

Uses the supplied fixture as authoritative repository context, may re-check that evidence during execution, and does not invent file contents, package-manager commands, or exact paths that the fixture does not provide.
Uses an ordered, risk-driven workflow rather than a static checklist and does not bypass material missing evidence, incompatible capability, failed validation, or unsafe authority.

Enforces authorization at server/data boundaries, makes prerender/reconnect side effects idempotent, avoids parallel use of one DbContext, models circuit recovery, and selects render-mode APIs only from the pinned target framework and installed component capabilities.

Names the fixture-provided focused test, affected test, type-check, and build categories, states exact command names come from the manifest and none ran, and makes completion depend on the required checks without inventing a package manager.

Reports enough hypothetical repository context to ground the decisions or proposed changes, not-yet-executed checks and expected acceptance evidence, residual risks, and unresolved external boundaries without inventing results.
Keeps optional provider or version detail subordinate and loads a linked reference only when needed; does not expand into a neighboring skill's primary ownership.

scenarios.prompt: A Blazor admin action is hidden in UI but callable, prerender invokes it twice, and reconnect retries after an ambiguous response. Explain the safe server contract, persistence boundary, and regression evidence.

assertions.criterion: Before any material mutation, resolves applicable exact targets, authority or permissions, ownership, and recovery or rollback. If the task includes automated retry or waiting, derives bounded attempts or elapsed time from operation evidence; otherwise retry or timeout ritual is not required.
Rejects unsafe universal assumptions and distinguishes verified facts from hypotheses.
Uses caller-visible or persisted outcome evidence and does not treat configuration or command success alone as proof.
Does not invent a framework version or version-gated API when the task provides no release context.

scenarios.prompt: Use blazor-development in an existing project whose manifests and lockfiles pin an older supported release. A newer stable release also exists. Choose compatible guidance without silently upgrading.

assertions.criterion: Uses installed manifests, lockfiles, runtime files and capability evidence for an existing project; treats an upgrade as a separate migration.

Checks the cross-stack compatibility dimensions applicable to the selected repository, such as engine, peers, compiler/framework, test runner, or deployment runtime, without demanding irrelevant dimensions.
Verifies a selected command or API with at least one applicable capability source such as installed/generated types, CLI help, configuration schema, or matching official documentation.

scenarios.prompt: Start a greenfield project that needs blazor-development. No manifest or lockfile exists yet. Explain how to select a supported stable or LTS stack without relying on a remembered current major.

assertions.criterion: Resolves stable or LTS release data at execution time from the configured official sources, checks cross-stack compatibility, and lets the generated manifest and lockfile become authority.
